subject: Exec flash: priority flashcards + QBR prep
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Exec Leadership <exec@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Exec flash: priority flashcards + QBR prep

Good morning — quick flash update for the leadership distro (wins / risks / asks) as we lock QBR slides. Short and actionable.

Wins:
- Throughput improvements: Serving runtime infra reduced 99th percentile latency for small-chat traffic by ~18% after the microkernel patch (validated on staging).
- Customer wins: Acme pilot completed integration smoke tests; embeddings volume expected +22% next quarter.
- Ops: Dedicated pool autoscaler now supports burst policies; early traffic shaping reduced token costs in test env by 12%.

Risks / open issues:
- SQL perf regression: a small uptick in tail latency for long-context reranking queries observed in canary (root cause points to a KV-cache eviction edge case). Mitigation in flight but could impact a small set of enterprise workloads if not contained.
- QBR readiness: two slides (SLA incident timeline; unit-econ adjustments) need finalized numbers from Finance & Platform by EOD Thu to avoid last-minute deck churn.

Asks (specific):
1) Vivek / Jonas — recommend canary rollback option be prepared (runbook attached) and an on-call validation window tomorrow 9–10a PT. Can you confirm?
2) Laura — need final wording for the SLA exception we plan to propose to Acme; single para for slide by Wed noon please.
3) Exec distro — please flag any additional asks for the QBR doc link below; I will consolidate into a single slide.

Attachments: [Attachment: QBR-Flashcards-v2.pptx (slides stub)]
Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=QBR-Flashcards-v2

Thanks — I kept this intentionally short.

—
Mina Haddad

Looping in Jonas and infra SRE. I agree with prep for a rollback runbook and a short validation window. I've attached the suggested rollback runbook (minimal, step-by-step) and proposed canary gating checks.

Proposed plan:
- Today: SRE reviews runbook + canary metrics (jonas)
- Tue 9–10a PT: on-call validation (prod read-only checks, smoke load at canary routing)
- Tue 11a PT: decision checkpoint for rollback vs patch-forward

Jonas — can you confirm SRE bandwidth for these times? If yes, I will block calendar and notify the on-call rotation.

Folks — quick follow-up and answers to the asks. Keeping to the slide-length responses for the QBR deck.

SQL perf regression (one-line slide phrasing):
- Impact: tail latency increase (~200–300ms) for long-context reranking observed in canary; affects ~3% of enterprise tenant traffic (no sign of Acme in current diagnostics). We have a targeted patch and rollback option; validation tomorrow 9–10a PT.

Canary rollback runbook:
- Runbook prepared and attached (rollback_runbook.pdf). Vivek/Jonas confirmed SRE review window and bandwidth.

SLA slide numbers:
- Incident window: 2027-02-18 02:15–03:40 UTC (majority customer impact cleared by automated fallback).
- Unit econ adj: updated per finance input; final numbers posted on the drive link below.

Final ask list (to be consolidated into one QBR slide):
- Laura: SLA slide paragraph (requested) — please drop a single-paragraph approval or edit by Wed 12:00 PT.
- Finance: confirm final unit-econ numbers by Thu EOD (cc finance in follow-up).
- Exec distro: review slides in the Drive and flag any additional high-level items by Wed EOD.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=QBR-Flashcards-v2
